answer.rationale: memory_c2 shows a prior low-cost-vendor migration succeeded with fast onboarding, clean invoicing, and sharp unit-cost reduction—exactly what the 18% mandate requires. memory_c6 confirms the incumbent's volume-pricing benefit has already been exhausted (incumbent refused to reopen price), so renewal adds no cost path forward. I flag that memory_c2 describes a past migration; the present line is at 94% with zero buffer, so the primary residual risk is a delivery gap during handoff. Because only one decision can be made this cycle, I am choosing to switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor whose quote alone meets the mandate, while contractually conditioning the cutover on a parallel delivery overlap window with the incumbent's 14-day wind-down to avoid a hard switchover into a bufferless line. The 14-day expiry window and the incumbent's refusal to move on price close off renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms as viable cost paths; add_second_source and defer_decision both leave the mandate unmet and, in the defer case, expose us to a lapse.
